transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-09-10 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (CTO), Liam (ML Eng), Janelle (DevOps)

00:00:03 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, I'm Maya, I'm the AE on the Redwood side, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. how's everyone?
00:00:12 - Priya: Good, thanks. we're excited to learn more. we've been evaluating hosted vs dedicated for inference and wanted to see the quickstart experience for the PLG API piece.
00:00:25 - Diego: Great. high level, I'll cover time-to-first-token, quickstart flow, free credits, and then dig into any infra/security constraints you have.
00:00:36 - Liam: Awesome, for context, we're building an internal semantic search + code generation feature for our analytics product. main things: latency targets <= 300ms for short responses, cost needs to be controlled, and we have some regulatory needs
ddata residency and audit logs.
00:00:55 - Janelle: And our infra team prefers VPC-first deployments. if private is required, need to understand effort.
00:01:05 - Maya: Perfect. quick qualification 
how many requests per second are we talking and what's the expected payload (avg tokens)?
00:01:12 - Priya: Maybe 30
60 QPS at peak for embedding lookups, prompts around 80
150 tokens for generation. throughput for embeddings is higher.
00:01:25 - Diego: Okay that maps to both hosted and dedicated options. hosted gives fastest time-to-value
you sign up, get API keys and free credits we put in the account, and you can be sending your first token within minutes. dedicated is better for predictable throughput and cost isolation, private (VPC/on-prem) for residency and extra control.
00:01:46 - Liam: Quick question: what is the typical onboarding time for self-serve? i.e., how many minutes to first token if we follow quickstart?
00:01:55 - Maya: In our PLG experience, time-to-first-token is usually under 15 minutes
signup, SDK install, set API key, run the quickstart sample. we also have templates for embeddings, chat, and streaming.
00:02:08 - Priya: And the free credits, how large are they? will they let us load test?
00:02:14 - Diego: We typically provision trial credits sufficient for basic benchmarks
depends on the program but enough to run some throughput tests. for heavier benchmarking we coordinate with growth ops to allocate more or we set up a short pilot on Dedicated.
00:02:26 - Janelle: On VPC/private: how much setup complexity are we looking at? is there a customer-managed control plane or do you host the control plane?
00:02:34 - Maya: For Redwood Private we do a customer-managed networking option. control plane can be private or hybrid; for on-prem we ship a package. integration points: SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM for keys, and audit logs for compliance. setup time varies
small evals can be weeks, full on-prem months depending on approvals.
00:02:55 - Priya: SOC2 is a must. do you have SOC2 and ISO artifacts we can review?
00:03:01 - Maya: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 docs; we will share them post-call.
00:03:06 - Liam: What's the data retention / logs policy for hosted? do you retain prompts?
00:03:12 - Diego: By default, hosted has configurable retention. for many customers we support no-retention or short retention modes and encryption at rest. for full separation we recommend Dedicated or Private which gives stronger isolation and data separation.
00:03:26 - Priya: Cool. cost side 
per-token pricing, and do you offer batching or KV cache suggestions?
00:03:32 - Maya: Yes, pricing is per-token for generation and per-embedding unit for embeddings. our Optimize tooling suggests batching and KV cache configs; SEs can run through suggested quantization/models to balance latency vs cost.
00:03:45 - Liam: Speaking of KV, we've heard about a KV cache in the runtime; any notes on that?
00:03:50 - Diego: Our runtime has prefix and KV cache optimizations
the transcript here might say K V cash sometimes
yea, it reduces cost for repeated contexts. we also support model variants and fallbacks to keep SLOs.
00:04:02 - Priya: Any self-serve limits or rate-limits in the free trial?
00:04:07 - Maya: Trials often have quotas and rate limits to protect the system. we'll supply a trial quota and if you need higher we can lift temporarily during benchmark window.
00:04:16 - Janelle: Network egress and VPC peering 
does Private support customer VPC peering or is it a VPN?
00:04:23 - Diego: Private supports both VPC peering and VPN depending on cloud and policy. we'll share the network diagram.
00:04:31 - [00:04:31] 
4m mark 
natural pause, folks checking docs.
00:04:55 - Priya: Walk me through the quickstart sample code for embeddings 
i want to see how much work to switch from our current client.
00:05:02 - Diego: sure, sample is a curl + python + node SDK snippet. curl: you set API_KEY in header POST to /v1/embeddings with model param, and response contains vectors. python SDK wraps that with a single call. we have a plg quickstart repo and a template that you can copy.
00:05:20 - Liam: Do you do streaming for generation? we need token-level streaming for incremental UI updates.
00:05:25 - Maya: yes, streaming responses are supported in hosted and dedicated. function/tool calling and structured outputs also available.
00:05:33 - Priya: For enterprise controls, we need RBAC and audit logs
who can create keys, who can rollout model changes?
00:05:40 - Diego: Redwood Console has RBAC, per-route/model dashboards, and audit trails. for Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your SSO for provisioning and have role-based access control.
00:05:52 - [00:05:52] Liam: What about model catalog and what models are pre-curated?
00:05:58 - Maya: We curate open models and verify performance profiles. also provide suggestions for quantization profiles. for some customers we host privately licensed models.
00:06:08 - Priya: Any partner hardware
GPUs like A100x, H100?
00:06:12 - Diego: Dedicated runs on a mix depending on region
usually H100 for low-latency configs but we select kernels and compilation per model.
00:06:20 - Janelle: Security question 
KMS/HSM integration for customer-managed keys?
00:06:25 - Maya: Yes, we support KMS/HSM integration for Private and Dedicated; hosted supports customer-managed keys for encryption at rest in certain tiers.
00:06:34 - [00:06:34] Priya: If we start self-serve, what's the typical path to upgrade to Dedicated? is it seamless?
00:06:41 - Diego: We try to make rollout seamless. you can pin model versions and route traffic; canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback to hosted if dedicated capacity is constrained. migration involves capacity planning.
00:06:55 - Priya: Great. any concerns with our token limits 
e.g., 2k vs 16k context windows?
00:07:02 - Maya: We support multiple sequence lengths depending on model; you pick models from catalog. if you need long context we can recommend long-context models and config.
00:07:12 - Liam: Could we run a quick live test? even a small demo sending an embed and a small generation?
00:07:17 - Maya: Sure, we can do a mini quickstart. I'll paste a curl in chat
i'll paste a placeholder link.
00:07:26 - [Screen share / paste sample curl]
00:07:35 - Diego: (reads sample) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' -d '{"model":"redwood-embedding-1","input":"open source search"}'
00:07:46 - Liam: we don't have an API key yet.
00:07:48 - Maya: Right
i'll provision trial creds after this call. for now i'll show expected responses and latencies from our quickstart benchmarks.
00:07:58 - Diego: Example latency for our small test model on hosted is ~60
120ms for embeddings and 120
350ms for small generation depending on prompt size.
00:08:08 - Priya: Good baseline. can you share a small benchmark spreadsheet?
00:08:12 - Maya: yes, we'll attach the benchmark spreadsheet and sample scripts.
00:08:16 - [00:08:16] cross talk 
short interruptions as Maya types links.
00:08:30 - Janelle: If we go Dedicated, how do upgrades and patching work?
00:08:35 - Diego: We handle runtime upgrades; for Dedicated we coordinate maintenance windows, and for Private we can support your patching cadence.
00:08:44 - Priya: Any SLA numbers for Dedicated?
00:08:47 - Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; details in the enterprise pack. we'll send the SLA summary.
00:08:55 - Liam: For model monitoring, do you provide quality/regression alerts? we need to detect quality drift post-rollout.
00:09:02 - Diego: Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring tied to prompt sets/evals and regression alerts. you can push evals and set thresholds.
00:09:12 - Priya: Great. On the compliance side, is there support for audit logs export to our SIEM?
00:09:18 - Maya: Yes, audit logs can be exported via S3/Kafka or pushed to SIEM depending on configuration.
00:09:26 - [00:09:26] quick pause.
00:09:40 - Priya: ok walk me through the cost controls
how do we cap spend per route, tokens?
00:09:47 - Diego: We have per-route quotas, token caps, and rate limiting. Console shows token-level cost breakdown. you can set hard caps to stop usage past thresholds.
00:09:58 - Janelle: For our security review we usually require a network diagram and a data flow. can you share that?
00:10:03 - Maya: Yes, we'll attach the network diagram and a dataflow doc.
00:10:10 - Liam: Any pitfalls when switching from OpenAI APIs to Redwood? client changes?
00:10:15 - Diego: We've seen minimal friction
SDKs are similar in design. we provide migration guides and quickstart repos. some differences in model names and options but easy to adapt.
00:10:26 - Priya: What about model licensing or bringing your own model?
00:10:30 - Maya: You can bring your own model on Dedicated/Private. on hosted we serve curated models and licensed ones depending on agreements.
00:10:38 - [00:10:38] 10m mark - Diego shares slide with quickstart steps.
00:10:45 - Diego: Quickstart steps: 1) Sign up and verify org, 2) Install SDK or curl sample, 3) Set API key, 4) Run sample calls (embed/generate), 5) Run benchmark script against trial quota, 6) Elevate to pilot if needed.
00:10:59 - Priya: What's the typical duration of a pilot?
00:11:03 - Maya: Pilots are commonly 2
6 weeks depending on scope.
00:11:07 - Liam: Could we do a 2-week POC for embeddings and basic generation and then evaluate Dedicated?
00:11:11 - Maya: That's a common path. we'll provide trial credits and help run benchmarks.
00:11:16 - Janelle: Any legal/terms we should expect for pilots?
00:11:20 - Maya: Standard trial terms; for Dedicated/Private there are enterprise agreements. procurement can be looped once you decide.
00:11:28 - Priya: Ok, let's talk about next week 
who should be involved for the benchmark session?
00:11:33 - Liam: Myself for load tests, Janelle for networking, and Diego for Redwood's side to run scripts.
00:11:39 - Diego: Sounds good. we'll bring a small test harness and load script.
00:11:43 - Maya: i'll schedule a 60-min benchmark session and send invites.
00:11:48 - [00:11:48] short sync on calendar.
00:12:05 - Priya: Any concerns about model drift and privacy? we send PII in prompts sometimes.
00:12:12 - Diego: For PII we recommend token-level filters, PII redaction in client, and using Private/Dedicated with customer-managed keys for highest assurance. also content filtering options exist.
00:12:25 - Priya: Ok good. cost optimization
quantization recommendations?
00:12:30 - Diego: Yes, Optimize surfaces quantization suggestions per workload
sometimes an 8-bit or 4-bit quantized model gives good perf/cost tradeoff. we'll run an analysis during the pilot.
00:12:41 - [00:12:41] small interruption as Priya reads a doc.
00:12:58 - Maya: quick recap: we'll send pricing + SOC2 + network diagram + benchmark spreadsheet. we'll provision trial credits and schedule the benchmark session. you (Priya) will share prompt sets and success criteria.
00:13:11 - Priya: Sounds good. any blockers on our side to start the self-serve trial?
00:13:17 - Janelle: I need to confirm whether the trial needs VPC access or if we can start with hosted.
00:13:21 - Maya: You can start hosted for fastest time-to-first-token and if it meets needs we can scope Dedicated. if compliance requires, we can open Private eval.
00:13:31 - Liam: ok let's do hosted quickstart first.
00:13:33 - Priya: agreed.
00:13:35 - Maya: great 
next steps I have captured and will follow up via email with artifacts and trial provisioning.
00:13:42 - [00:13:42] wrap up and thanks.
